To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a high-resolution structure of a G-quadrupex containing ALS and FDT related GGGGCC repeats was determined by NMR.
a G-quadruplace structure formed by a d[(G4)3GG(B)GG] DNA oligonucleotide with a single G to 8BrG substitution has been solved by NMR spectroscopy.
the GGGGCC repeat in C9orf72 is able to fold into a single G-quartet containing structure in the presence of potassium ions, and that this structure can be stabilized by 8Br-dGuo substitution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the structure and function of G-quadruples in the expanded GGGGCC repeats, which are involved in the development of ALS and FTD.
the investigation of the structure, dynamics and thermodynamic stability of G-quadruplices formed by the C9orf72 GGGGCC repeat.
the structure of G-quadrupules containing GGGGCC repeat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this G-quadrupLEX structure is a model for the GGGGCC repeat containing quadruplexes, which are proposed to play important roles in the pathogenesis of ALS and FTD.
the DNA quadruplex structure of the GGGGCC repeat region is a very stable structure, which is stabilized by stacking of loop nucleotides onto the G-quartets.
G-quadruple structures formed by the shortest model of C9orf-72 GGGGCC repeat are very stable and compact and can be stabilized by single 8Br-dGuo substitution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have determined the structure of the shortest DNA oligonucleotide with the ability to fold into G-quadruples and that this structure can be used as a starting point for further studies on the structure of longer oligonucleotidesthat can potentially fold into more complicated structures.

the GGGGCC repeat can adopt a variety of G-quadruples structures and the structure of the most stable one is highly dependent upon the number of repeat units, the length and sequence of flanking regions, as well as the presence of K+ ions.
the structure of G-quadrupex containing GGGGCC repeat is highly compact and stable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the G-quadruple structures of GGGGCC repeats may have an important role in the pathogenesis of ALS/FTD.

the G-quadruplix structure adopted by the d[(G4)4] repeat is very similar to the structure adopted by the repeat containing 8Br-dGG substitution, which indicates that the G-quartets formed by the repeat units are not significantly perturbed by the presence of 8Br-dgg.
G-quadruple structure of the GGGGCC repeat is very compact and stable and that the presence of a single 8-bromo-substituted dG residue at the position 21 is sufficient to stabilize this structure.
